title: wulfhilde map
description: A map of the wulfhilde engine, in a file ending .map.json: sectors bounded by loops of walls, portals that link them, and where the player starts. Units are metres, in right-handed coordinates with Z up, and every coordinate lies within 4,096 m of the origin on each axis. The engine checks the same rules when it loads a map, and more that a schema can't state: a key written twice, a number too near zero to read, the winding and crossing of loops, inner loops outside the outer loop or inside each other, sector and wall ids that repeat, references to sectors and walls that don't exist, a portal's walls that don't run between the same corners in opposite directions, a wall that is a side of two portals, an exposure range whose minimum is above its maximum, and nits on a surface whose material doesn't emit.

$schema.description: The schema that an editor checks the file against. The engine ignores it.

format.description: What the file is: a wulfhilde map.

version.description: The version of the map format the file is written in. This version of the engine reads version 1 only.

ambient.description: The ambient light of every sector that doesn't set its own. Without it, ambient light is black.

exposure.description: The exposures the map is seen at, as a camera's EV at ISO 100, where a higher EV100 takes in less light: about 15 for a sunlit yard, and about 5 for a room lit indoors. Exposure is metered from what the camera sees, within the range.

min.description: The lowest exposure, for the darkest places, in EV100, no higher than max. Defaults to 1.

max.description: The highest exposure, for the brightest places, in EV100. Defaults to 16.

compensation.description: How many stops brighter than the metered exposure the map is seen, or darker below 0. Defaults to 0.

portals.description: The map's portals, each of which links two walls so that each wall's sector is seen and reached through it from the other's.

start.description: Where the player is placed when the map loads, and which way they face.

number.description: A number within the range the engine reads numbers in, that of a single-precision float.

planPoint.description: A point seen from above, [x, y], in metres.

point.description: A point, [x, y, z], in metres.

assetPath.description: The asset path of an asset: its file's path under the content root, in /-separated segments of a-z, 0-9, _ and -, without the extension that the kind of asset supplies.

color.description: A colour in linear Rec.709, [r, g, b], each component from 0 to 1.

properties.description: Game-defined data, which the engine keeps and ignores.

ambientLight.description: Light that arrives equally from every direction, the same everywhere in a sector, on top of any lights.

color.description: The light's colour, which filters white.

lux.description: The illuminance the light gives a surface facing any way, in lux.

materialPath.description: The asset path of the material that covers the surface, a file ending .material.json under the content root.

offset.description: How far the material is moved along u and v, in metres. Defaults to [0, 0].

scale.description: What the material's real-world size is multiplied by, along u and v. Defaults to [1, 1].

rotation.description: How far the material is turned in the surface's plane, in degrees, from +u toward +v, about the point its offset moves its origin to. Its scale applies along its own turned axes. Defaults to 0.

surfaceNits.description: The luminance of the material's emission at white, in nits, in place of the material's own. It changes the emission's brightness, not its colour or its pattern, and only a material that emits may take it.

surface.description: The material that covers a wall, and how it lies on it: u runs along the wall from its start, to the right as the wall is seen from its sector, and v is height.

sky.description: A sky, which shows an infinitely distant backdrop instead of a material. The backdrop is fixed to the sector's coordinates.

backdrop.description: The asset path of the backdrop, a file ending .backdrop.json under the content root, in /-separated segments of a-z, 0-9, _ and -, without the extension.

nits.description: The luminance of the backdrop's white, in nits, in place of the backdrop's own.

floorOrCeiling.description: A sector's floor or ceiling: the height it lies at, and either the material that covers it, with u and v along X and Y, or a sky, but not both.

height.description: The height it lies at, in metres.

wall.description: A wall, which runs from its own start to the start of the next wall in its loop, the last wall to the first, and stands from the sector's floor to its ceiling. A wall that is a side of a portal is open where the sector beyond overlaps its own, and solid only on its strips above and below.

id.description: The wall's name, unique among the map's walls, by which a portal refers to it. A wall that nothing refers to needs none.

start.description: Where the wall starts, seen from above.

upper.description: The surface of the wall's upper strip, above its opening where the sector beyond has a lower ceiling, if the wall is a side of a portal. Defaults to the wall's surface.

lower.description: The surface of the wall's lower strip, below its opening where the sector beyond has a higher floor, if the wall is a side of a portal. Defaults to the wall's surface.

sector.description: A region bounded by an outer loop of walls and any number of inner loops around holes in it, with a floor below and a ceiling above. Sectors may share the same space.

id.description: The sector's name, unique in the map, by which the start position refers to it.

ambient.description: The sector's own ambient light, in place of the map's.

loops.description: The sector's loops of walls: the outer loop first, which runs anticlockwise seen from above, then any inner loops, each around a hole in the sector and running clockwise. No loop crosses or touches itself or another, each inner loop lies inside the outer loop, and none lies inside another. Any loop may be concave. Each wall faces into the sector, which lies to its left.

portalSide.description: A side of a portal: a wall, by its id. This version of the engine links walls only.

portal.description: A portal, which links side a to side b. Its walls lie in different sectors and run between the same corners in opposite directions, and the sector beyond each is seen and reached through its opening, from the higher floor to the lower ceiling. A wall is a side of one portal at most.

sector.description: The id of the sector the player starts in.

point.description: Where the player's feet are, in the sector's coordinates.

yaw.description: How far the player's facing turns left from +X, anticlockwise seen from above, in degrees.

pitch.description: How far the player's facing tilts up from the horizontal, in degrees. Defaults to 0.
